---
title: "Missing values"
---

A missing quantity means that a protein group was not quantified in that sample;
it does not establish that the protein was absent. After [quality control](qc.html)
and [normalization](normalization.html), decide whether to leave those gaps or
impute selected values.

::: {.alert .alert-warning role="note"}
**Imputation is optional:** Use this approach when treating undetected signals as
low abundance makes sense for your experiment. Imputed values are estimates.
:::

This example continues with the HepG2 protein-group `se` from
[Preparing data](preparing-data.html), using the imported DIA-NN quantities.
Keep the intensities on their original scale; do not log-transform them first.

```{r setup, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(ProteoVaultR)
library(dplyr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
data_dir <- Sys.getenv("PROTEOVAULTR_DEMO_DIR", unset = "demo-data")
vault <- open_vault(
    file.path(data_dir, "hepg2_ifna-dia.proteovault.duckdb")
)
sample_info <- tibble::tribble(
    ~sample_name,   ~sample_id, ~condition,
    "Control_R1",  "Ctrl1",    "Control",
    "Control_R2",  "Ctrl2",    "Control",
    "Control_R3",  "Ctrl3",    "Control",
    "IFNa_12h_R1", "IFNa1",    "IFNa",
    "IFNa_12h_R2", "IFNa2",    "IFNa",
    "IFNa_12h_R3", "IFNa3",    "IFNa"
)
sample_info$condition <- factor(
    sample_info$condition, levels = c("Control", "IFNa")
)
vault <- set_sample_metadata(vault, sample_info)
se <- as_summarized_experiment(vault, method = "matrix")
close_vault(vault)
```

## 1. Apply conditional imputation

Conditional imputation uses consistency across replicates to decide when a
low-abundance estimate may be reasonable. For example, a protein quantified in
all three controls but none of the IFNa samples may have fallen below reliable
quantification after treatment. Filling that wholly missing condition makes this
pattern available for comparison.

Requiring repeated observations helps keep isolated detections from driving the
comparison. The low-abundance interpretation remains an assumption; imputation
does not establish why the measurements are missing.

Use `condition` to group biological replicates. For each protein group, the
default behavior is to:

- Keep a condition with at least two observed replicates, leaving any remaining
  gaps missing (`observed`).
- Fill a wholly missing condition only when another condition has at least two
  observed replicates (`lod_imputed`).
- Otherwise, set the whole condition to missing (`insufficient`), including any
  single observed value.

The fill value is a sample-specific limit-of-detection (LOD) estimate: half the
smallest positive intensity observed in that sample. Zeros are treated as missing.

```{r conditional-imputation}
se_imputed <- impute_conditional_lod(se, bin = "condition")
SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(se_imputed)
```

The original `quantity` assay is retained. The new `quantity_imputed` assay
contains the result, including gaps that were left missing or masked.

For additionally normalized data, use `se_genorm` and set
`assay = "quantity_genorm_normalized"` instead.

## 2. Check what changed

The result records a status for each protein group in each condition. Summarize
those statuses before continuing:

```{r imputation-status}
SummarizedExperiment::rowData(se_imputed) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    count(imputation_status_Control, imputation_status_IFNa, name = "protein_groups") %>%
    knitr::kable(col.names = c("Control", "IFNa", "Protein groups"))
```

For later analysis, select `assay = "quantity_imputed"` if you want to use these
values. Keep the original assay for comparison. Next, compare conditions with
[Differential abundance](differential-abundance.html).
